hook.line: Google just released a spam update aimed at people manipulating generative AI.
hook.visual: Selfie-cam walk outdoors in bright sun, orange title box 'Google Update Aims to Punish GEO Tactics' over his head, white captions with orange word highlight.

beats.what: News hook: spam update targets GEO manipulation, orange headline box on top
First jump cut; title box gone, context on how Google links spam policies
Reveals the new policy section against manipulating AI results
Names the two tactics: Reddit comments and paid publisher recommendations
Argues detection is hard: how could Google know who placed a recommendation
Turn: AI cites the same pages, so a few surgical placements matter
Proof story: one placed recommendation took a client from 20% to 40% of tracked prompts
Verdict: targeted placement is safe, recommendation building is the new link building

why_it_works: Timely news hook ('just released') plus a threat ('penalty') makes SEO viewers stay to learn if they are at risk
Orange headline box states the whole topic in the first frame, so a muted scroller knows what the video answers
A concrete client result (20% to 40% of tracked prompts from one placement) is held back until the end, rewarding viewers who stayed
Fast talk (3.76 words/s) with almost no silence (7.6%) keeps momentum despite few cuts
weaknesses: 137 s with only 6 cuts and no cutaways: the picture barely changes, long shots up to 40.5 s
Headline box disappears after the first cut, leaving nothing but captions to anchor the topic
No call to action at all
The proof claim is only spoken; no screenshot or number on screen
for_robert: Copy the orange headline box with the topic as a question-shaped claim in frame one, but put the proof number on screen (Fred holding a '20% to 40%' sign) instead of only saying it.
